newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses hit by Wall St fears,dollar down.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses hit by Wall St fears,dollar down.

text.p: European shares suffered a renewed bout of jitters on Wednesday morning amid concern over the next move on Wall Street, the world's biggest stock market.
Losses in key Asian markets led the way as futures prices pointed to a pronounced drop when the New York market opens, recalling the market mayhem at the end of last week.
The dollar also lost ground, jolted by widening of more than 31 percent in Japan's October trade surplus with the United States, mainly due to a boost in vehicle exports.

"The current account data from the U.S. and Japan highlight the way that the Japanese current account surplus is being effectively recycled and suggest some problems for the dollar if overseas investors become less attracted to the U.S. asset markets," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica in London.

London share traders said a reversal in market sentiment, after two days of recovery in share prices, was largely due to a Wall Street Journal article suggesting that a slowdown in Japanese purchases of U.S. debt could depress U.S. markets.
This hit exchanges which had clawed their way back from sharp losses after remarks by U.S. central bank chief Alan Greenspan on the "irrational exuberance" of the U.S. stock market.
Weaker bond prices made their contribution, too, while investors were also nervous ahead of U.S. November producer prices due at 1330 GMT.
Economists expect November's U.S. producer prices to show a rise of 0.3 percent after October's 0.4 percent gain. Any faster increase would raise fears of higher interest rates.

The FTSE 100 index of blue-chip stocks in London, Europe's leading stock market, dipped below the key 4,000 level soon after the start before reviving a little but then slipping back again to show a loss of one percent by mid-morning.

"London will be hard pressed to make any progress today," one trader said. "Wall Street didn't finish as nicely as we left it here in London and bonds are down. We had a poor finish in Japan and people could be expecting another wobble starting from the Far East."

The Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue chips closed 9.31 points higher at 6,473.25 on Tuesday after being up 28 points as London markets closed. A U.S. market rally was restrained by selling of technology shares.
French and German shares lost more than one percent in early business in sympathy with other stock markets and amid investor concern that Wall Street might have peaked after a record-breaking run.
In Asian trading, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 closed 253.74 points or 1.22 percent lower at 20,568.38, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 152.86 points or 1.15 percent to 13,189.60.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.90 yen and 1.5440 marks against 113.29 and 1.5539 in late European business on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 39.8 points lower at 3,995.9
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 28.43 at 2,222.97.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt fell 44.94 to 2,846.06.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold rose to $369.75 an ounce, compared with Tuesday's close of $368.25. Silver gained to $4.86 versus $4.81.
